native_chart_classification.explanation: Existing native fallback requires transactions == ext_msgs_accepted and gas==0. Signed16-child NTRN parents have16 logical transactions per accepted external envelope, so all nonempty native rows are omitted from native-only charts. Native accepted counter provides independent evidence of logical count; do not hardcode16 in the fix.

client_static_profile.meaning: More connections divide the existing logical window; they do not multiply it. Smaller per-client credits can reduce native parents per RPC and increase admission overhead. Actual current runtime settings and counters are needed to establish whether this limit is binding.

validator_static_profile.meaning: Budgets are upper bounds. Four shard collations, serialized actor stages, dormant parallel-trie thresholds and waits do not automatically consume48cores. Work-driven basechain production skips target-rate sleeps; configured300ms is not a fixed basechain TPS cap in that mode.

bottleneck_inference: Sustained observed production is about48.6k–51.7k logicalTPS in the chosen windows despite distinct unlabelled bursts; this does not establish a10vs300 causal comparison.

Native execution is1.58–1.84 wall microseconds/transfer while collation commonly waits101–169ms per block for incoming eligible work. This points toward ingestion/scheduling/credit availability as the next measurement target, rather than raw native-transfer execution or physical link bandwidth.

Later bursts mostly wait for first work (for example134.602ms of157.471ms total external wait at06:14). That await follows an empty local queue; it does not identify whether B is underfeeding, A admission is slow, snapshot retries are delaying messages, or the producer actor is waiting to publish already pending work.

At9a587bc1 A rejects asynchronous NTRN admission when whole masterchain snapshot ID changes and also on source-account revisions. Previous invalid test retry counts cannot establish the current rate of those races. Measure current not_ready_by_reason, RPC RTT, client logical credits and server admission timings before changing these correctness guards.
Mean accepted blocks contain only2.1k–3.4k logical transfers in the selected plateaus even though some reach18432. The queue ceiling is not a demonstrated universal per-block saturation constraint.

Accepted block data is roughly79–84bytes per logical transfer in those windows, consistent with only about32–34Mbps of block data at50kTPS; this is block serialization, not a measurement of client wire bytes or total network utilization.
